messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight 'capability token' for service-to-service auth to reduce our API key blast radius and simplify per-route RBAC. Short-lived, signed, optionally bound to org/project and route claims.
ajay: Sounds promising. Two quick questions: 1) latency/overhead for every call if we validate signatures? 2) how do we handle high QPS services?
sasha: +1 on the idea but worried about migration churn. Lots of services assume long-lived API keys today. We need a pragmatic fallback plan.
ken: Implementation notes: tokens minted by a central broker (auth-service), signed with HSM-backed key. Validation can be done by local public key cache to avoid HSM calls. TTL: 1–15m typical, refresh via short-lived session.
emily: Rollout idea: start with path-level opt-in. Services accept old API keys and capability tokens side-by-side. Canary route rejects API keys and logs reasons for a week before enforcing.
maria: Tradeoffs: pro — small blast radius, easier least-privilege mapping to routes; con — more moving parts (broker, rotation, caching). Also need to measure added CPU for signature checks.
ajay: For QPS, we can use signature verification with cached JWKs and hardware accel. Also consider mac-based tokens (HMAC) for internal-only paths to be cheaper than asymmetric verify.
sasha: Migration steps request: 1) broker spec + API, 2) library (go/py) for minting/validation, 3) infra: JWK distribution + rotation hooks, 4) phased opt-in + canary, 5) enforcement.
ken: Edge cases: background jobs that run offline (no refresh) — we should allow bounded long-lived tokens for batch workers scoped to project with strict TTL and rotation policy. Also tenant-affinity header to prevent cross-tenant reuse.
emily: Observability: emit token-type, minting-principal, route-claim, and audit-id. Add regressions guard: if errors spike >5% during canary, automatic rollback to accept-api-key mode for that route.
maria: Security questions: do we embed org/project in claims or derive it at validation time? I vote embed with audience claims to make intent explicit and enable cheap validation.
ajay: Embed org/project but require broker to sign an attestation that includes a short-binding proof. Also include 'origins' claim to prevent replay from other regions.
sasha: Perf test plan: create a harness that validates 10k rps for both HMAC and RSA/EC variants, measure p95 CPU and latency. We should also benchmark cache stamps (JWK rotation) effect.
ken: SDK example (draft):
```
// mint request
POST /v1/mint
{ "service": "ingest-worker", "routes": ["/v1/ingest"], "ttl": 300 }
// token (jwt) claims
{ "iss":"auth-broker", "sub":"svc:ingest-worker", "aud":"/v1/ingest", "org":"org-123", "exp":1719200300 }
```
ops-bot: Deploy note: created feature-flag "capability-auth" in staging. Use `ff toggle capability-auth on --env=staging` to opt-in.
emily: Can we add a compatibility header `X-Accepted-Credential: api-key|capability` to make logging simpler?
maria: Yes — please include that in SDKs.
ken: Next actions: I'll draft broker API + JWK rotation doc. Sasha, can you own migration playbook? Emily, own canary + rollback wiring. Ajay, perf harness. Maria will write security appendix (attestation details).
sasha: On it. I'll draft playbook with timelines and mitigation for offline workers.
ajay: I'll start the perf harness tomorrow and share results by EOW.
emily: I'll add observability metrics to the rollout checklist.
maria: +1. If no blockers, we'll spin up a short RFC PR with the broker API tomorrow. :thumbsup:
